shortDescription: A tall storage basket with handles. Great for holding yarn, magazines, or toys.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked in the round with simple increases.

yarn.notes: Use a stiff super bulky yarn or hold two strands together.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines basket size.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 4, join. Round 1: 8 sc into ring. Increase to 32 sc over 4 rounds.
**Walls:** Chain 1, sc in BACK loop only of each stitch. This creates the base-to-wall corner.
**Rounds 2-14:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around. Work even for 13 rounds.
**Handles (Round 15):** Chain 1, sc in next 10, chain 12, skip 6, sc in next 10, chain 12, skip 6, sc in remaining 10. Join.
**Round 16:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch and each chain around. Join.
**Round 17:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around. Join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The back-loop round is essential for the basket to stand up.
Basket handles should be long enough to fit over your arm.
Two strands held together make a stiffer basket.
commonMistakes: Skipping the back-loop first wall round — basket collapses.
Making the handles too short to carry comfortably.

name: Super Bulky Dog Mat
shortDescription: A thick, cushy mat for your dog to sleep on. Quick to make and machine washable.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked flat; no shaping needed.

yarn.notes: Machine washable yarn is a must for pet items.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines mat size.

instructions: **Mat:** Chain 40 (or desired width).
**Row 1:** Sc in 2nd chain from hook and each across. (39 sc), turn.
**Rows 2-40:** Chain 1, turn. Sc in each stitch across. (39 sc each row)
**Border:** Sc evenly around the entire rectangle, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Rounds 2-3:** Sc in each stitch around, with 3 sc in each corner stitch. Join.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Make the mat as wide as your dog is long.
Add a non-slip fabric coating to the bottom if using on hardwood floors.
This mat is just a big rectangle — the easiest project in the catalog.
commonMistakes: Making the mat too small — measure your dog first.
Skipping the corner increases in the border (3 sc in each corner keeps it flat).

name: Super Bulky Wreath
shortDescription: A quick seasonal wreath made by covering a foam wreath form with super bulky yarn.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked around a wreath form; no shaping required.

yarn.notes: Use seasonal colors — orange for fall, red/green for Christmas.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for a wreath.

instructions: **Covering:** Chain 4, join. Sc in each chain. Work in a continuous spiral, increasing as needed to keep the tube flat.
**Continue:** Slip the tube over the wreath form as you go. The tube should wrap around the form snugly.
**Seam:** When the wreath form is fully covered, fasten off. Sew the ends of the tube together neatly.
**Decoration:** Add a bow, artificial flowers, or ornaments using hot glue.
**Hanging loop:** Attach a 6-inch chain loop at the top.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: A foam wreath form from a craft store costs $2-3.
Change colors seasonally for a year-round decoration.
Add dried lavender or eucalyptus for a natural touch.
commonMistakes: Making the tube too narrow to fit over the wreath form.
The covering bunching up — smooth it as you go.

name: Jumbo Halloween Pumpkin
shortDescription: A giant floor pumpkin made with jumbo yarn. Perfect fall decoration that works up fast.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in the round; the shape comes from stuffing and cinching.

yarn.notes: Orange jumbo yarn for the pumpkin body, brown or green for the stem.

notions: Small piece of brown or green yarn for stem

gauge.notes: Gauge determines pumpkin size.

instructions: **Body:** Chain 4, join. Round 1: 8 sc into ring. Increase to 24 sc over 3 rounds.
**Rounds 4-10:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around. Work even for 7 rounds.
**Rounds 11-12:** Decrease by sc2tog evenly around each round. Stuff firmly before closing.

**Cinch (creates pumpkin segments):** Thread a long piece of yarn through the center (top to bottom), pull tight, and wrap around the outside. Create 6 segments by repeating 6 times around the pumpkin.
**Stem:** With brown yarn, chain 4, sc in 2nd chain and each. Sew to top center of pumpkin.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The cinching creates the classic pumpkin ribbed look.
Make a set in different sizes for a fall display.
Add a curly vine by chaining 20 and slip stitching back.
commonMistakes: Not stuffing firmly enough — the pumpkin should be dense.
Uneven cinching makes the segments look lopsided.

name: Jumbo Door Stop
shortDescription: A heavy, sand-filled doorstop covered in jumbo yarn. Keeps doors open without slipping.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked flat; a simple rectangle folded and seamed.

yarn.notes: Durable, heavy yarn.

notions: Small ziplock bag filled with sand or gravel

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Outer cover:** Chain 12.
**Row 1:** Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (11 sc), turn.
**Rows 2-20:** Chain 1, sc in each across. (11 sc each row)
**Fold and seam:** Fold rectangle in half to form a wedge. Slip stitch the long edge and one short edge, leaving one short edge open.
**Insert sand bag:** Place the sand-filled ziplock bag (wrapped in fabric) inside.
**Close:** Slip stitch the remaining edge closed.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The sand bag must be securely sealed — double-bag for safety.
A heavier door needs a larger sand bag.
This is the fastest project in the catalog — under 30 minutes.
commonMistakes: Sand bag leaking — always double-bag with a fabric inner layer.
Making the cover too small for the sand bag.

name: Jumbo Floor Ottoman
shortDescription: A large floor ottoman or pouf made with jumbo yarn. Use as extra seating or a footrest.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet in the round with shaping for a cylindrical form.

yarn.notes: Use firm jumbo yarn that holds its shape.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines ottoman size.

instructions: **Top:** Chain 4, join. Round 1: 8 sc into ring. Increase by 8 stitches each round until circle is about 18 inches across.
**Sides (Round 1):** Chain 1, sc in BACK loop only of each stitch. This creates the corner.
**Rounds 2-18:** Chain 1, sc in each stitch around. Work even for 17 rounds.
**Bottom:** Decrease by 8 stitches each round until opening is small.
**Stuff:** Insert pillow forms or poly-fil before closing completely.
**Close:** Sc2tog around until closed. Fasten off.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use old pillows for stuffing to save money on poly-fil.
The back-loop round is critical for the walls to stand up.
Make the top circle larger for a wider ottoman.
commonMistakes: Not using the back loop for the first side round — the ottoman collapses.
Under-stuffing — the ottoman should be firm enough to sit on.

name: Pineapple Lace Doily
shortDescription: A large, intricate pineapple doily with multiple lace layers. A showpiece project.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chains, double crochet, treble crochet, picots, and pineapple stitch motif.

yarn.notes: Mercerized cotton thread (size 10).

gauge.notes: Gauge is important for doily size.

instructions: **Center:** Chain 10, join. Work 24 dc into ring.
**Rounds 1-10:** Establish 8 pineapple segments around the center. Each pineapple is built from a chain-3 base with increasing dc clusters and picot tips.
**Rounds 11-25:** Continue each pineapple outward, adding chain loops and picots between segments. The doily grows to about 18 inches across.
**Outer edge:** Work a scalloped border: *7 dc in next chain space, skip 1, sl st in next.* Repeat around.
**Finishing:** Fasten off. Block and starch firmly. Pin each picot point flat while drying.
beginnerTips: This is an advanced doily — practice on a smaller doily first.
Use a stitch marker on every round; it's easy to lose track.
Starching is essential — the pineapple segments need stiffness.
commonMistakes: Losing count of chain loops between pineapples.
Not pinning picots flat during blocking.

name: Cabled Slouchy Beret
shortDescription: A slouchy beret with intricate cable stitches. Looks like knitting but is crochet.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses front-post and back-post treble crochet to create cable crosses.

yarn.notes: Worsted weight with good stitch definition.

gauge.notes: Gauge is critical for hat fit.

instructions: **Band:** Chain 24. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. Work sc in back loop only for 40 rows (or until band fits around head). Sew ends together.
**Body:** Pick up and sc evenly around the band (about 72 stitches).
**Cable setup:** *Fpdc in next 4, bpdc in next 2.* Repeat around. (12 cables, 12 background sections)
**Cable row:** Skip 2 fpdc, fpdc in next 2, then fpdc in the skipped 2 (cable cross). Bpdc in next 2. Repeat around.
**Rounds 3-10:** Continue cable pattern, crossing cables every 4th round.
**Crown decreases:** *Fpdc2tog across each 4-st cable, bpdc in next 2.* Repeat until 12 sts remain.
**Finishing:** Cut yarn, pull through remaining stitches, and secure. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Practice the cable cross on a swatch before starting the hat.
Use a cable needle (or a small hook) to hold the skipped stitches.
A wool-blend yarn gives the best cable definition.
commonMistakes: Crossing cables in the wrong direction.
Not making the band long enough — it should stretch slightly to fit.

name: Irish Rose Motif
shortDescription: A three-dimensional Irish crochet rose motif. Can be used as an applique, brooch, or joined into larger projects.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chains, double crochet, and treble crochet in 3D layering technique.

yarn.notes: Mercerized cotton shows stitch definition best.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for a motif.

instructions: **Center (petal layer 1):** Chain 6, join. *Ch 4, tr in ring, ch 4, sl st in ring.* Repeat 4 times. (5 petals)
**Petal layer 2:** *In next ch-4 space from back: ch 5, dtr in same space, ch 5, sl st.* Repeat around behind layer 1.
**Petal layer 3:** *In next ch-5 space from back: ch 6, trtr in same space, ch 6, sl st.* Repeat around.
**Leaves (make 2):** Chain 8. Sc in 2nd chain, hdc in next, dc in next 2, hdc in next, sc in next, ch 3, sl st back through the chain. Work down the other side.
**Assembly:** Layer the petals. Sew leaves to the bottom of the rose. Attach a brooch pin to the back if desired.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Starch lightly to shape.
beginnerTips: The rose is built from the center outward — each layer is worked behind the previous one.
Use a smooth, mercerized cotton for the best stitch definition.
Spray starch helps the petals hold their shape.
commonMistakes: Working the next layer in front instead of behind the previous layer.
Pulling the petals too tight — they should cup naturally.

name: Bobble Stitch Baby Blanket
shortDescription: A textured baby blanket with bobble stitches forming a diamond pattern. Machine washable.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses bobble stitches, front-post stitches, and pattern reading.

yarn.notes: Machine washable worsted weight yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines blanket size.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 100.
**Row 1:** Dc in 4th chain and each across. (98 dc), turn.
**Row 2 (pattern setup):** Chain 3, dc in next 4, *bobble in next (5 dc in same st, drop loop, pull through), dc in next 7.* Repeat across, ending with dc in last 5. Turn.
**Rows 3-80:** Follow the diamond bobble chart: bobbles are offset each row to create diagonal lines. The chart repeats every 12 rows.
**Border:** Sc evenly around the entire blanket, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Round 2:** *Sc in next 3, ch 2 picot.* Repeat around.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Block to shape.
beginnerTips: The bobble stitch is: yarn over, insert hook, pull up loop (repeat 5 times), yarn over and pull through all loops on hook.
Use a stitch marker to mark the right side of the blanket.
Count your stitches after each bobble row to ensure accuracy.
commonMistakes: Bobbles too tight — they should pop out from the fabric.
Dropping the bobble loop and losing the stitch.

name: Intarsia Colorblock Bag
shortDescription: A structured bag with intarsia colorwork. Teaches carrying multiple yarn colors in one row.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses intarsia colorwork technique with multiple yarn bobbins.

yarn.notes: Main color: 150yds, contrast colors: 50yds each.

gauge.notes: Gauge is important for bag structure.

instructions: **Front panel:** Chain 36 in main color. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (35 sc), turn.
**Colorwork rows (rows 5-30):** Follow the intarsia chart. Use separate bobbins for each color section. Twist yarns at color changes to prevent holes. Each row has 2-4 color changes.
**Back panel:** Same as front, worked in solid main color.
**Side gusset:** Chain 8. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (7 sc). Continue in sc for 70 rows (or until gusset fits around front + back panels).
**Assembly:** Whip-stitch the gusset to the front and back panels.
**Lining:** Cut fabric lining to size and hand-sew inside the bag.
**Closure:** Attach magnetic snap to the center of the top edge.
**Straps (make 2):** Chain 80. Sl st in each chain back. Attach to bag with yarn needle.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Wind small amounts of contrast colors onto yarn bobbins before starting.
Twist the old and new colors at each change to prevent gaps.
A fabric lining gives the bag structure and hides the inside colorwork.
commonMistakes: Not twisting yarns at color changes, leaving holes.
Tangling bobbins — keep them organized by color position.
Uneven tension between colors.

name: Stained Glass Window Panel
shortDescription: A decorative crochet panel that mimics stained glass, using black yarn as leading and bright colors as glass.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses tapestry crochet technique with color changes on every stitch and precise tension control.

yarn.notes: Black for outlines (200yds), assorted bright colors for glass sections.

notions: Embroidery hoop or frame for display

gauge.notes: Gauge should be tight for a stiff panel.

instructions: **Set up chart:** The design is worked from a grid chart. Each square = 1 single crochet. Black stitches form the outline 'leading.' Color stitches fill the 'glass.'
**Foundation:** Chain 80 in black.
**Row 1:** Sc in 2nd chain and each across in black. (79 sc), turn.
**Row 2 (color starts):** Follow the chart. Work sc in sc, carrying the unused color inside the stitch. Change colors at the exact stitch indicated by the chart.
**Rows 3-80:** Continue following the chart. The black outlines are maintained throughout, with colors filling the defined sections.
**Carrying yarn:** When working a color section, carry the black yarn along the top of the row, crocheting over it. When working black, carry the color yarn.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Block firmly. Mount in an embroidery hoop or frame. Hang in a window for the stained glass effect.
beginnerTips: Practice tapestry crochet on a small swatch before starting the full panel.
The carried yarn should be visible on the back but hidden on the front.
Tension is everything — keep it tight and even.
Use a stitch marker on every row to track color changes.
commonMistakes: Inconsistent tension — the carried yarn shows through on the front.
Losing count on the chart — use a row tracker or magnetic chart holder.
Choosing colors with too little contrast against the black outlines.

name: Zippered Pouch
shortDescription: A lined pouch with a zipper closure. Perfect for makeup or travel essentials.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet and requires sewing in a zipper.

yarn.notes: Cotton holds shape well for zippered pouches.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines pouch size.

instructions: **Front:** Chain 20. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (19 sc). Work even for 20 rows.
**Back:** Repeat front.
**Lining:** Cut fabric to match crochet pieces plus seam allowance. Sew lining to wrong side of each piece.
**Zipper:** Place zipper face-down between front and back pieces. Whip-stitch securely through all layers.
**Sides:** Fold right sides together, slip stitch sides and bottom closed.
**Finishing:** Turn right-side out. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use a contrasting zipper for a pop of color.
A zipper foot on a sewing machine makes this much easier.
commonMistakes: Zipper installed upside-down.
Stitches catching in the zipper teeth.

name: Knit-Look Pouch
shortDescription: A pouch with a knit-like texture using waistcoat stitch. Sturdy and elegant.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses waistcoat stitch (yarn-over sc through center of post) for a knit-like fabric.

yarn.notes: Smooth yarn shows waistcoat stitch best.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines pouch size.

instructions: **Panel (make 2):** Chain 18. Work waistcoat stitch in 2nd chain and each across. (17 sts). Work even for 22 rows.
**Waistcoat stitch:** Insert hook through the center of the stitch post (between the V), yarn over, pull up loop, yarn over, pull through both loops.
**Assembly:** Whip-stitch three sides together. Attach magnetic snap to the top edge of each panel.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Block lightly to even stitches.
beginnerTips: Waistcoat stitch is tighter than regular sc — use a slightly larger hook.
Practice on a swatch first; the stitch is different from standard sc.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to work through the center post rather than the top loops.

name: Fair Isle Mug Cozy
shortDescription: A colorwork mug cozy with a Fair Isle-inspired pattern. Uses tapestry crochet technique.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses tapestry crochet with color changes in the round.

yarn.notes: Main color 25yds, contrast color 15yds.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines fit around mug.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 35 (or mug circumference). Join.
**Rounds 1-3:** Sc in each stitch in main color.
**Rounds 4-8:** Follow Fair Isle chart: alternate between main and contrast color every 2 stitches, carrying unused yarn inside.
**Rounds 9-10:** Sc in each stitch in main color. Button loop: chain 5 on last row, skip 2 stitches.
**Finishing:** Fasten off. Sew button opposite loop. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Carry the unused color loosely — tight floats will pucker the fabric.
Use bobbins for contrast colors to prevent tangling.
commonMistakes: Carrying yarn too tight, causing the cozy to be too small.

name: Beaded Plant Hanger
shortDescription: A macrame-inspired plant hanger with wooden beads threaded onto chain stitches.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain stitch with beads threaded on.

yarn.notes: Cotton rope or sturdy cotton yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Top ring:** Chain 4, join.
**Straps (make 4):** Thread 3 beads onto yarn. Chain 50, sliding a bead into place every 10th chain stitch.
**Attach straps:** Slip stitch each strap to the top ring.
**Knot:** About 6 inches from bottom, tie all straps together. Add a final bead over the knot.
**Finishing:** Trim ends evenly.
beginnerTips: Thread all beads onto the yarn before starting to chain.
Use a bead with a hole large enough for your yarn.
commonMistakes: Beads too small for the yarn — test before threading.

name: Tassel Keychain
shortDescription: A colorful tassel keychain that works up in minutes. Great for using scrap yarn.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain stitch and wrapping; no crochet experience needed.

yarn.notes: Scrap yarn works perfectly.

notions: Small piece of cardboard (3 inches wide)

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Tassel:** Wrap yarn around 3-inch cardboard 20 times. Cut a 6-inch piece of yarn and tie tightly around the top. Cut the bottom loops. Trim evenly.
**Cap:** Chain 6. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (5 sc). Work back and forth for 4 rows. Fold around tassel top and whip-stitch edges together.
**Attach:** Slip stitch the cap to the keychain ring.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Use multiple colors for a striped tassel effect.
Trim the tassel ends perfectly even for a polished look.
commonMistakes: Tassel cap too loose — it should grip the tassel tightly.

name: Beaded Name Wristband
shortDescription: A personalized wristband with letter beads. Great for camp, events, or gifts.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain stitch and slip stitch.

yarn.notes: Any scrap yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 8. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (7 sc). Work even for 20 rows.
**Bead panel:** On the next row, work sc but thread a letter bead onto the yarn before each stitch. Work the bead snug against the fabric.
**Button loop:** Chain 6 at one end, slip stitch back to form a loop.
**Finishing:** Sew button opposite loop. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Thread beads onto the yarn in reverse order (last letter first).
Pre-thread all beads before starting the bead row.
commonMistakes: Beads too small for the yarn — check hole size.

name: Padded Eyeglass Case
shortDescription: A padded eyeglass case with a soft lining to protect lenses. Sturdy and functional.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked flat with a folded design.

yarn.notes: Cotton holds shape well.

notions: Felt or fleece for lining (6x8 inches)

gauge.notes: Gauge determines case size.

instructions: **Outer:** Chain 16. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (15 sc). Work even for 30 rows.
**Fold:** Fold rectangle in half (short ends together). Slip stitch side edges closed.
**Lining:** Cut felt to same size as outer (15x30 stitches). Insert into case.
**Flap:** Chain 1, sc in next 8 stitches. Work even for 6 rows for the flap. Button loop: chain 4, skip 2, sc in last 2.
**Finishing:** Sew button opposite loop. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Measure your glasses before starting to ensure a good fit.
Felt lining provides extra padding without sewing.
commonMistakes: Case too short — glasses should fit completely inside with the flap closed.

name: Crossbody Phone Pouch
shortDescription: A hands-free phone pouch with an adjustable crossbody strap. Perfect for walks and travel.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked flat with a simple strap.

yarn.notes: Sturdy yarn works best.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines phone fit.

instructions: **Pouch:** Chain 20 (or phone width). Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (19 sc). Work even for 25 rows.
**Flap:** Sc in next 10 stitches only for the flap. Work 8 rows. Button loop on row 8: chain 5, skip 2, sc in last 3.
**Strap (make 2):** Chain 100. Slip stitch back along the chain. Attach to sides of pouch.
**Finishing:** Sew button opposite loop. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Measure your phone width and add 1 inch for ease.
Make the strap adjustable by sewing a button on each end.
commonMistakes: Phone pouch too tight — your phone should slide in and out easily.

name: Wine Bottle Gift Bag
shortDescription: A festive wine bottle bag with a drawstring top. Perfect for hostess gifts.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in the round.

yarn.notes: Festive colors — red, green, gold.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines bag size.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 4, join. 8 sc into ring. Increase to 32 sc over 4 rounds.
**Body:** Sc in each stitch around. Join. Work even for 20 rounds.
**Drawstring holes:** *Sc in next 3, chain 2, skip 2.* Repeat around. Join.
**Top:** Sc in each stitch and chain for 3 more rounds.
**Drawstring:** Thread ribbon through the chain-2 spaces.
**Finishing:** Pull ribbon to close. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: A standard wine bottle is about 12 inches tall — adjust bag height accordingly.
Use a decorative ribbon for the drawstring.
commonMistakes: Diameter too small — the bag should fit around the bottle with some ease.

name: Knotted Turban Headband
shortDescription: A stylish knotted turban headband with a pre-made knot sewn in place. Quick and trendy.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet; the knot is created by folding and sewing.

yarn.notes: Soft, stretchy yarn works best.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines headband fit.

instructions: **Band:** Chain 8. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (7 sc). Work even for 50 rows (or until band fits around head).
**Knot piece:** Chain 6. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (5 sc). Work even for 8 rows.
**Assembly:** Fold the knot piece in half widthwise. Wrap the center of the band with the knot piece and sew the ends together at the back.
**Finishing:** Sew the short ends of the band together. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Measure your head before starting to ensure the band is the right length.
Use a contrasting color for the knot piece.
commonMistakes: Band too short — it should stretch slightly but not be tight.

name: Foldable Shopping Tote
shortDescription: A lightweight tote that folds into its own pocket. Perfect for keeping in your purse.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet and double crochet; works flat.

yarn.notes: Light but strong yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines tote size.

instructions: **Body:** Chain 30. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (29 sc). Work sc for 30 rows.
**Pocket (for folding into):** Chain 30. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (29 sc). Work for 10 rows.
**Straps (make 2):** Chain 60. Slip stitch back along the chain. Attach to top edge of body.
**Assembly:** Sew pocket to one side of the tote, leaving top open. The tote folds into this pocket.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The pocket should be wide enough to hold the folded tote.
Use a light, strong yarn — bulky works up fast.
commonMistakes: Pocket too small for the folded tote.

name: Corner Bookmark
shortDescription: A cute corner bookmark that slips over the page corner. Quick and adorable.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in a small triangle shape.

yarn.notes: Scrap yarn is perfect.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Start:** Chain 12.
**Row 1:** Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (11 sc), turn.
**Row 2:** Chain 1, sc2tog, sc in next 7, sc2tog. (9 sc), turn.
**Row 3:** Chain 1, sc2tog, sc in next 5, sc2tog. (7 sc), turn.
**Row 4:** Chain 1, sc2tog, sc in next 3, sc2tog. (5 sc), turn.
**Row 5:** Chain 1, sc2tog, sc in next 1, sc2tog. (3 sc), turn.
**Row 6:** Chain 1, sc3tog. Fasten off.
**Pocket edge:** Sc evenly along the two straight edges to form the pocket that slips over the page corner.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Add a pom-pom or tassel to the point for decoration.
Make a set as a gift — they use almost no yarn.
commonMistakes: Decreasing too fast, making the bookmark too short.

name: Ankle Bootie Slippers
shortDescription: Warm ankle-height bootie slippers with a ribbed cuff. Felted for extra durability.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet with heel and toe shaping; worked in the round.

yarn.notes: 100% wool (not superwash) if felting.

gauge.notes: Gauge before felting.

instructions: **Sole (make 2):** Chain 20. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (19 sc). Increase at both ends every row until sole is 27 sts wide. Work even for 15 rows.
**Heel:** Work heel flat on 14 stitches for 8 rows. Fold and seam.
**Upper:** Pick up stitches around the sole. Sc in each stitch around for 15 rounds.
**Cuff:** Sc in back loop only for 8 rounds to create a ribbed ankle cuff.
**Felt (optional):** Machine wash hot, cold rinse, dry on high. Shape while damp.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Trace your foot and compare the sole before felting.
Felted slippers shrink — make them 20% larger than your foot.
commonMistakes: Using superwash wool that won't felt.
Slippers too small after felting.

name: Kids Hooded Poncho
shortDescription: A cozy hooded poncho for kids. Easy to put on and take off — no buttons or zippers.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only double crochet worked in a simple rectangle with a hood.

yarn.notes: Soft, warm bulky yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines poncho size.

instructions: **Back:** Chain 60. Dc in 4th chain and each across. (58 dc). Work even for 30 rows.
**Front:** Same as back.
**Hood (make 2):** Chain 30. Dc in 4th chain and each across. (28 dc). Work even for 20 rows.
**Assembly:** Whip-stitch shoulder seams (leave 10-inch neck opening). Sew hood pieces together at top, then sew to neck opening.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Add fringe along the bottom edge (optional).
beginnerTips: Make the neck opening large enough for the child's head to fit through.
Fringe adds a fun touch and uses up scrap yarn.
commonMistakes: Neck opening too small — the poncho won't go over the child's head.

name: Shell Stitch Baby Blanket
shortDescription: A sweet baby blanket with a shell stitch border. Soft and elegant.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses double crochet and shell stitch (5 dc in same stitch).

yarn.notes: Soft baby yarn in a pastel shade.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines blanket size.

instructions: **Blanket:** Chain 90. Dc in 4th chain and each across. (88 dc). Work even for 60 rows.
**Shell border (round 1):** *Skip 2, 5 dc in next, skip 2, sl st in next.* Repeat around. At corners: 5 dc, ch 2, 5 dc in the same stitch.
**Shell border (round 2):** *Sl st in next 2, 5 dc in next sl st, sl st in next 2.* Repeat around.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The shell border adds 3-4 inches to the blanket size.
Count your shells at each corner to keep them even.
commonMistakes: Uneven shell spacing on the border — mark corner positions with stitch markers.

name: Mosaic Coaster Set
shortDescription: A set of 4 coasters with a mosaic tile look, using short row colorwork.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses mosaic crochet technique with short rows and color changes.

yarn.notes: 2 colors per coaster, 15yds each.

gauge.notes: Gauge is forgiving.

instructions: **Setup (Color A):** Chain 16. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (15 sc), turn.

**Row 1 (Color B):** Ch 1, sc in first 2 stitches. *Drop B, pick up A (do not cut), sc in same stitch (the dropped loop will be covered later).* Drop A, pick up B. Alternating creates the mosaic effect.
**Rows 2-14:** Continue following the mosaic chart: working short rows and carrying unused color.
**Edge:** Sc evenly around all 4 sides with Color A, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Make 4 coasters total.
beginnerTips: Mosaic crochet creates geometric patterns without complicated stitches.
Each coaster uses only 2 colors — pick high-contrast pairs.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to carry the unused color — it should be visible on the back only.

name: Lace Napkin Rings
shortDescription: Elegant napkin rings made with lace thread. A set of 4 for special occasions.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chains, double crochet, and picots in the round.

yarn.notes: Mercerized cotton thread (size 10).

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Ring (make 4):** Chain 40. Join with slip stitch.
**Round 1:** Dc in each chain. Join. (40 dc)
**Round 2 (picot):** *Sc in next 2, ch 3, sl st in first ch (picot), skip 1.* Repeat around.
**Finishing:** Fasten off. Starch lightly and shape over a napkin ring form. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Make all 4 rings identically for a cohesive look.
Starching helps the rings hold their shape.
commonMistakes: Rings too loose — use a smaller hook if necessary.

name: Lace Angel Ornament
shortDescription: A delicate angel ornament for the Christmas tree. Makes a cherished heirloom.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chains, double crochet, treble crochet, and picots with 3D shaping.

yarn.notes: White mercerized cotton thread.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Head:** Chain 4, join. 8 sc into ring. Work even for 3 rounds. Stuff lightly.
**Skirt:** Work 3 dc in each stitch around head. (24 dc). Continue with shell stitch *5 dc in next, skip 2* for 5 rounds.
**Wings (make 2):** Chain 10. *Tr in 4th chain from hook, ch 3, sl st in same chain.* Repeat for wing shape.
**Halo:** Chain 15, sl st back. Attach to head.
**Assembly:** Sew wings to back. Attach a ribbon for hanging.
**Finishing:** Starch and shape. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Starch the skirt firmly so it flares out.
Use a very small amount of stuffing for the head.
commonMistakes: Wings too small — they should extend past the skirt.

name: Lace Edging Sampler
shortDescription: A sampler of 5 different lace edging patterns. Practice new stitches on small swatches.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chains, double crochet, treble crochet, and picots.

yarn.notes: White cotton thread.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Edging 1 (Shell):** Chain foundation. *Skip 2, 5 dc in next, skip 2, sl st in next.*
**Edging 2 (Picot):** *Sc in next 3, ch 4, sl st in 4th chain from hook.*
**Edging 3 (Fan):** *Skip 2, (dc, ch 1) 4 times in next, skip 2, sl st in next.*
**Edging 4 (Scallop):** *Skip 1, 7 tr in next, skip 1, sl st in next.*
**Edging 5 (V-stitch):** *Skip 2, (dc, ch 2, dc) in next, skip 2, sl st in next.*
**Finishing:** Practice each edging on a 6-inch chain. Keep for reference.
beginnerTips: This is a practice piece — keep it in your project bag as a stitch reference.
Label each edging with a safety pin tag.
commonMistakes: Skipping the slip stitch between repeats — it keeps the edging flat.

name: Hairpin Lace Scarf
shortDescription: A scarf made with hairpin lace technique. Lightweight, airy, and beautifully textured.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses hairpin lace technique with a loom; requires specialized equipment.

yarn.notes: A soft, drapey lace yarn.

gauge.notes: Width is fixed by loom size.

instructions: **Setup:** Set hairpin lace loom to 2-inch width. Tie yarn to left prong.
**Strip 1:** Work hairpin lace across loom for 120 loops. Remove from loom.
**Crochet center:** Insert hook through loops on one side, ch 3 between each loop to create the center spine.
**Repeat:** Make 3 strips total. Join strips by whip-stitching the outer loops together.
**Finishing:** Block to open the lace. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Hairpin lace creates a distinctive spiral edge on both sides.
A narrower loom makes a denser fabric.
commonMistakes: Loops uneven in size — keep tension consistent across the loom.

name: Fingering Bookmark
shortDescription: An intricate bookmark in super fine yarn. Makes a thoughtful handmade gift.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and double crochet in a small repeat.

yarn.notes: Scrap fingering weight yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 14.
**Row 1:** Dc in 4th chain from hook. *Ch 1, skip 1, dc in next.* Repeat across. Turn.
**Row 2:** Ch 4, *dc in next dc, ch 1.* Repeat across. Turn.
**Repeat Row 2:** Continue for 30 rows.
**Tassel:** Cut 12 pieces of yarn 4 inches long. Fold in half and loop through the bottom chain space.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Trim tassel evenly.
beginnerTips: The open mesh pattern uses very little yarn.
A tassel at the bottom adds a classic bookmark look.
commonMistakes: Tassel too thick — 12 strands is plenty for this width.

name: Fingering Baby Hat
shortDescription: A lightweight baby hat in super fine yarn. Perfect for spring and newborn photos.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet in the round with crown decreases.

yarn.notes: Soft, non-irritating yarn for baby.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines hat size.

instructions: **Start:** Chain 4, join. 8 sc into ring. Increase to 48 sc over 6 rounds.
**Body:** Sc in each stitch around. Work even for 20 rounds.
**Brim:** Sc in back loop only for 4 rounds.
**Crown decreases:** *Sc in next 6, sc2tog.* Repeat around. Continue decreasing until 8 sts remain. Cut yarn, pull through, secure.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Add a pom-pom (optional).
beginnerTips: A newborn hat should be about 12 inches in circumference.
The back-loop brim creates a rolled edge.
commonMistakes: Hat too small — add an extra increase round for a larger size.

name: Fingering Lace Scarf Pin
shortDescription: A decorative knit/crochet shawl pin made by crocheting around a wooden dowel.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and single crochet around a dowel.

yarn.notes: Lustrous fiber looks best.

notions: 3-inch wooden dowel or large knitting needle

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Cover dowel:** Sc over the dowel, working stitches around it to cover completely. About 30 sc across.
**Decorative end:** Ch 10, sl st back to form a loop. Sew to one end of the covered dowel.
**Finishing:** Secure ends with a dab of hot glue. Weave in yarn ends.
beginnerTips: The dowel should be smooth so the crochet cover slides on easily.
Add a bead to the decorative loop for extra elegance.
commonMistakes: Crochet cover too loose — use a smaller hook or tighter tension.

name: Fingering Cotton Blouse
shortDescription: A lightweight summer blouse in fingering weight cotton. Boxy fit with lace sleeves.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses double crochet and lace pattern with garment shaping and seaming.

yarn.notes: Fingering weight cotton/linen blend.

gauge.notes: Gauge is critical.

instructions: **Front:** Chain 80. Dc in 4th chain and each across. (78 dc). Work even for 40 rows. Shape neckline at center.
**Back:** Same as front but without neck shaping.
**Sleeves (make 2):** Chain 40. Work lace pattern (dc, ch 1, skip 1) for 30 rows, increasing at edges every 5 rows.
**Seaming:** Whip-stitch shoulders, sides, and sleeves.
**Collar:** Sc evenly around neckline. Work 4 rounds of sc.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Block to measurements.
beginnerTips: This is a committed project — break it into sections.
A linen-cotton blend has beautiful drape for summer wear.
commonMistakes: Sleeve increases uneven — mark increase rows with stitch markers.

name: Sport Mesh Market Bag
shortDescription: A stretchy mesh market bag in sport weight cotton. Holds more than it looks like it can.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only chain and double crochet in a simple mesh.

yarn.notes: Sport weight cotton is strong and washable.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Bag:** Chain 50. Dc in 4th chain and each across. (48 dc). Work mesh pattern (*dc, ch 1, skip 1*) for 40 rows.
**Fold and seam:** Fold in half. Slip stitch sides together.
**Straps (make 2):** Chain 100. Slip stitch back. Attach to top edge.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. The bag stretches significantly when loaded.
beginnerTips: This bag is deceptively large — a little yarn goes a long way.
Cotton sport weight makes a strong, durable bag.
commonMistakes: Making the mesh too tight — the bag should be stretchy.

name: Sport Leg Warmers
shortDescription: Cozy leg warmers in sport weight yarn. Perfect for dance, yoga, or cold mornings.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in the round with ribbed cuffs.

yarn.notes: Stretchy yarn with good memory.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines fit.

instructions: **Cuff:** Chain 28. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (27 sc). Work even for 5 rows. Sew short ends to form a cuff.
**Leg (make 2):** Chain 36, join. Sc in each stitch around for 40 rounds (or desired length).
**Bottom cuff:** Sc in back loop only for 5 rounds.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Attach the top cuffs to each leg warmer.
beginnerTips: Try the leg warmer on as you go — add or skip rounds for the perfect length.
The back-loop cuffs create a stretchy, ribbed edge.
commonMistakes: Making the leg too narrow — it should fit over the calf.

name: Sport Baby Bonnet
shortDescription: A vintage-style baby bonnet in sport weight yarn. Ties under the chin with ribbon.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet with shaping for the crown and brim.

yarn.notes: Soft, washable baby yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines bonnet size.

instructions: **Crown:** Chain 4, join. 8 sc into ring. Increase to 40 sc over 5 rounds.
**Body:** Sc in each stitch around. Work even for 15 rounds.
**Brim:** Sc in first 20 stitches only (work flat). Decrease at both edges every row for 5 rows.
**Ties:** Chain 40 from each side of the brim. Slip stitch back along each chain.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Thread ribbon through the eyelet row (optional).
beginnerTips: A newborn bonnet has a crown circumference of about 12 inches.
Ribbon ties make it adjustable.
commonMistakes: Bonnet too shallow — add more rounds to the body section.

name: Sport Fingerless Mitts
shortDescription: Lightweight fingerless mitts in sport weight yarn. Great for cool mornings or typing.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in the round with a thumb hole.

yarn.notes: Warm but lightweight.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines fit.

instructions: **Cuff:** Chain 24, join. Sc in each stitch around. Work even for 6 rounds.
**Hand:** Sc in each stitch around for 8 rounds.
**Thumb hole:** Sc in next 18 stitches, chain 4, skip 4, sc in remaining 2 stitches. Join.
**Continue:** Sc in each stitch and each chain around. Work for 4 more rounds.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Repeat for second mitt.
beginnerTips: Try the mitt on as you go to check fit.
The thumb hole should be at the base of your thumb.
commonMistakes: Thumb hole too small — 4 chains is minimum for most thumbs.

name: Chunky Slouchy Toque
shortDescription: A trendy slouchy toque in bulky yarn. Deep fold-up brim for extra warmth.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in the round.

yarn.notes: Soft bulky yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines hat size.

instructions: **Brim:** Chain 28. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (27 sc). Work even for 30 rows. Sew short ends to form a band.
**Crown:** Pick up and sc evenly around the band (about 48 sc). Sc in each stitch around for 12 rounds.
**Decrease:** *Sc in next 6, sc2tog.* Repeat around. Continue decreasing until 8 sts remain.
**Finishing:** Cut yarn, pull through remaining stitches, pull tight. Weave in ends. Fold brim up.
beginnerTips: The folded brim adds warmth and style.
Make the band longer for a deeper fold.
commonMistakes: Crown too tight — the hat should sit loosely on the head.

name: Bulky Hooded Cowl
shortDescription: A hybrid hood-and-cowl in bulky yarn. Keeps your head and neck warm in one piece.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only double crochet worked flat and seamed.

yarn.notes: Warm, soft bulky yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is forgiving.

instructions: **Hood:** Chain 40. Dc in 4th chain and each across. (38 dc). Work even for 20 rows. Fold in half and sew top seam.
**Cowl:** Pick up stitches along the bottom of the hood. Dc in each stitch around (in the round) for 10 rounds.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. The cowl section sits around the neck, the hood covers the head.
beginnerTips: This is essentially a hood with an extended neck.
Try it on as you go to check the hood depth.
commonMistakes: Hood too shallow — it should cover the top of the head comfortably.

name: Bulky Basketweave Pillow
shortDescription: A decorative throw pillow with a basketweave texture. Front and back in contrasting colors.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses front-post and back-post double crochet in a basketweave pattern.

yarn.notes: Main color 120yds, contrast 60yds.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines pillow size.

instructions: **Front:** Chain 36. Setup: *fpdc in next 4, bpdc in next 4* repeat across. Work basketweave for 28 rows. Every 4 rows, swap fpdc/bpdc groups to create the weave.
**Back:** Same as front but solid sc in contrast color.
**Seaming:** Whip-stitch three sides together. Insert pillow form. Whip-stitch fourth side closed.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The basketweave pattern is 4 fpdc + 4 bpdc, swapped every 4 rows.
A contrasting back adds visual interest when the pillow is turned.
commonMistakes: Losing count of fpdc/bpdc groups — use stitch markers between groups.

name: Super Bulky Pom-Pom Hat
shortDescription: A quick hat with a large faux-fur pom-pom. Works up in under an hour.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in the round.

yarn.notes: Super bulky yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines hat size.

instructions: **Start:** Chain 4, join. 8 sc into ring. Increase to 32 sc over 4 rounds.
**Body:** Sc in each stitch around for 10 rounds (or desired hat height).
**Brim:** Sc in back loop only for 3 rounds.
**Finishing:** Fasten off. Attach pom-pom to the top center. Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: A faux-fur pom-pom adds a luxurious touch.
This hat takes about 30 minutes — great for last-minute gifts.
commonMistakes: Hat too tall — a beanie should sit just above the ears.

name: Super Bulky Arm Socks
shortDescription: Long arm warmers that reach to the bicep. Dramatic and cozy for winter layering.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked in the round.

yarn.notes: Super bulky yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines fit.

instructions: **Cuff:** Chain 20, join. Sc in each chain. Work even for 4 rounds.
**Arm:** Sc in each stitch around. Increase 2 stitches evenly every 5th round to accommodate the forearm.
**Continue:** Work even until piece measures about 14 inches (or desired length to bicep).
**Thumb hole:** On the last 3 rounds, leave a 4-stitch gap at the thumb position by chaining 4 and skipping 4 stitches on one round.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Repeat for second arm sock.
beginnerTips: Try the arm sock on as you go — the forearm is wider than the wrist.
These are dramatic and cozy — great for outdoor photos.
commonMistakes: Not increasing for the forearm — the sock will be too tight.

name: Super Bulky Tree Skirt
shortDescription: A quick Christmas tree skirt in super bulky yarn. Made in 2 halves and seamed.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses half-circle shaping with increases; made in 2 panels.

yarn.notes: Red or green super bulky yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines skirt radius.

instructions: **Panel 1 (half circle):** Chain 4, join. 12 dc into ring. Increase by 12 stitches each round until half-circle measures 36 inches across the straight edge.
**Panel 2:** Repeat for second half.
**Assembly:** Sew Velcro strips along the straight edges of both panels. The two halves wrap around the tree base.
**Edge:** Sc evenly around the curved edge of both halves.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: The Velcro closure makes it easy to remove for storage.
A 36-inch diameter fits most standard Christmas trees.
commonMistakes: Not making the straight edge long enough — it should reach the tree trunk.

name: Jumbo Bath Mat
shortDescription: A thick, absorbent bath mat in jumbo yarn. Quick to make and machine washable.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet worked flat.

yarn.notes: Machine washable jumbo cotton yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines mat size.

instructions: **Mat:** Chain 24 (or desired width). Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (23 sc). Work even for 30 rows (or desired length).
**Border:** Sc evenly around all 4 sides, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Cotton jumbo yarn is absorbent and washable.
A 24x30-inch mat takes about 1 hour to make.
commonMistakes: Mat too small — a bath mat should extend past the width of your feet.

name: Jumbo Wreath Basket
shortDescription: A shallow basket that doubles as a wreath decoration. Fill with pinecones or ornaments.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses only single crochet in the round.

yarn.notes: Jumbo yarn in seasonal colors.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 4, join. 8 sc into ring. Increase to 32 sc over 4 rounds.
**Walls (Round 1):** Sc in BACK loop only of each stitch. This creates the corner.
**Rounds 2-6:** Sc in each stitch around. Work even for 5 rounds.
**Hanging loop:** Ch 20, attach to opposite side.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Fill with seasonal decorations.
beginnerTips: The back-loop round is essential for the walls to stand up.
Fill with pinecones for fall, ornaments for Christmas.
commonMistakes: Not using the back loop — the basket won't hold its shape.

name: Jumbo Cat Cave
shortDescription: A cozy cave bed for cats made with jumbo yarn. The opening creates a sense of security.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet in the round with a shaped opening.

yarn.notes: Soft, machine-washable jumbo yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines cave size.

instructions: **Base:** Chain 4, join. 8 sc into ring. Increase to 40 sc over 5 rounds.
**Walls:** Sc in back loop only. Work even for 6 rounds.
**Opening:** Chain 1, sc in next 20 stitches. Chain 1, turn. Work flat for 8 rows to create the cave opening.
**Roof:** Continue working in the round again, joining the top of the opening. Sc around for 6 more rounds, decreasing slightly to dome the top.
**Finishing:** Fasten off, weave in ends. Place on floor — your cat will find it.
beginnerTips: Cats love enclosed spaces — the opening should be just big enough for them to enter.
Place a soft blanket or pillow inside.
commonMistakes: Opening too small — a cat needs at least 6 inches wide.

name: Filet Crochet Wall Art
shortDescription: A piece of crochet wall art using filet crochet technique. A pattern of solid and open mesh squares forms an image.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses filet crochet (dc + ch) with a pattern chart requiring careful counting.

yarn.notes: White or ecru cotton shows the filet pattern best.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines finished size.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 100.
**Row 1:** Dc in 8th chain from hook (counts as first mesh). *Ch 2, skip 2, dc in next.* Repeat across. (32 meshes).
**Rows 2-40:** Follow the filet chart. Filled mesh = 3 dc. Open mesh = dc, ch 2, dc. The pattern forms an image (flower, heart, or geometric design).
**Border:** Sc evenly around all 4 sides. Work a picot edge: *sc in next 3, ch 3, sl st in first ch.*
**Finishing:** Block aggressively. Mount in a frame or embroidery hoop for hanging.
beginnerTips: Print the chart and use a row tracker — losing your place is easy in filet.
Blocking is essential to open the meshes evenly.
Cotton thread gives the crispest definition.
commonMistakes: Counting meshes wrong — mark every 10th mesh with a stitch marker.
Tension too loose causes the design to look distorted.

name: Mosaic Crochet Wrap
shortDescription: A geometric wrap made with mosaic crochet technique. Two colors, stunning design.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses mosaic crochet with short rows, color changes, and pattern reading.

yarn.notes: Main color 250yds, contrast color 200yds.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines wrap size.

instructions: **Foundation:** Chain 100 in main color.
**Mosaic pattern:** Every row uses one color. The other color is carried across and picked up every 2 rows. Short rows create the geometric pattern.
**Rows 1-80:** Follow the mosaic chart. Dropped stitches create diagonal lines that form diamonds, zigzags, or chevrons.
**Finishing edge:** Switch to main color. Sc evenly around all edges, working 3 sc in each corner.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Block to shape.
beginnerTips: Mosaic crochet is worked with one color per row — never two in the same row.
The unused color is simply dropped and picked up later — do not cut it.
Use high-contrast colors for the best design impact.
commonMistakes: Cutting the unused color instead of dropping it.
Short rows placed incorrectly — follow the chart carefully.

name: Broomstick Lace Cowl
shortDescription: A cowl made with broomstick lace technique. Large loops create a dramatic, lacy fabric.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses broomstick lace technique: large loops pulled up over a knitting needle or dowel.

yarn.notes: A smooth, sturdy worsted weight yarn.

hook.notes: Standard hook plus a US 15 (10mm) knitting needle or 1-inch dowel.

notions: US 15 knitting needle (or 1-inch diameter dowel, 12 inches long)

gauge.notes: Loop size is fixed by the dowel.

instructions: **Setup:** Chain 30. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (29 sc). Turn.
**Row 1 (broomstick):** *Pull up a loop on the hook, place it on the knitting needle.* Repeat across. (29 loops on needle).
**Row 2 (lock loops):** Insert hook through the first 5 loops on the needle. Yarn over, pull through all 5 loops. Ch 1. *Sc in the center of the 5-loop group, ch 1.* Repeat across.
**Row 3:** Sc in each stitch across the previous row. (About 29 sc). Turn.
**Repeat:** Alternate broomstick rows (Row 1-2) with sc rows (Row 3) until cowl measures about 18 inches.
**Seam:** Fold in half and whip-stitch short ends together.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: A US 15 knitting needle (or 10mm dowel) creates consistent 1-inch loops.
Keep loops loose on the needle — tight loops are hard to work into on the next row.
The broomstick side is the right side of the fabric.
commonMistakes: Pulling loops too tight on the needle — they should slide freely.
Losing count of loops in each group — always group 5 loops.

name: Join-As-You-Go Afghan
shortDescription: A modular afghan made of granny squares joined as you go. No seaming at the end.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses granny squares with join-as-you-go technique, increasing in complexity as squares are added.

yarn.notes: Multiple colors — 6-8 contrasting shades.

gauge.notes: Each square is approximately 6 inches.

instructions: **Square 1:** Make a basic granny square with 4 rounds. Fasten off.
**Square 2:** Make 3 rounds. On round 4, join to Square 1 by working dc into the corresponding chain-2 space of Square 1 at one corner.
**Continue:** Add squares in rows, joining each new square to its neighbors on round 4. Each square is joined on 1 or 2 sides.
**Layout:** Make 6 rows of 5 squares each (30 squares total).
**Border:** Sc evenly around the entire blanket. Work 2 rounds of sc, then 1 round of picot edging.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: The join-as-you-go technique eliminates seaming — each square is attached as it's made.
Plan your color layout before starting.
Keep tension consistent across all squares for a uniform look.
commonMistakes: Joining on the wrong side — make sure all squares face the same direction.
Running out of a color mid-project — buy extra from the same dye lot.

name: Beaded Crochet Wallet
shortDescription: A structured wallet with bead embellishment and a snap closure. Fits cards and cash.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet with bead threading, fabric lining, and snap installation.

yarn.notes: Mercerized cotton for stitch definition.

gauge.notes: Gauge is important for wallet structure.

instructions: **Outer wallet:** Chain 28. Sc in 2nd chain and each across. (27 sc). Work even for 40 rows.
**Bead row (row 20):** Before each sc, slide a bead up to the hook and work the stitch. The bead sits on the front of the fabric.
**Fold and seam:** Fold the rectangle to create the wallet shape (bottom and sides). Slip stitch edges together, leaving top open.
**Lining:** Cut fabric to match. Sew lining and insert into wallet. Whip-stitch to top edge.
**Snap closure:** Install magnetic snap at center of the top edge.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Thread all beads onto the yarn before starting the bead row (in reverse order).
A fabric lining gives the wallet structure and hides the back of the beads.
commonMistakes: Beads too small for the yarn — test with a single stitch first.
Snap installed crooked — measure center carefully.

name: Tunisian Crochet Pillow
shortDescription: A throw pillow using Tunisian simple stitch. The dense, woven-like fabric is perfect for home decor.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses Tunisian crochet technique: forward pass and return pass, with a specialized hook.

yarn.notes: Smooth worsted weight yarn.

hook.notes: Tunisian crochet hook (at least 10 inches long) size J (6mm).

gauge.notes: Gauge determines pillow size.

instructions: **Setup:** Chain 60 using Tunisian hook.
**Row 1 (forward pass):** Insert hook in 2nd chain, pull up loop. Repeat across. (60 loops on hook).
**Row 1 (return pass):** Yarn over, pull through 1 loop. *Yarn over, pull through 2 loops.* Repeat across. (1 loop remains on hook).
**Rows 2-70:** Repeat forward and return passes. The fabric grows as a dense, woven panel. (Tunisian simple stitch creates a fabric that doesn't curl).
**Panel 2:** Repeat for second panel.
**Assembly:** Whip-stitch three sides together. Insert pillow form. Whip-stitch fourth side closed.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Tunisian crochet requires a special hook — it's longer than a standard hook to hold all the loops.
Keep tension even on the forward pass — uneven loops create a wavy edge.
The fabric is reversible; both sides look similar.
commonMistakes: Losing loops off the end of the hook — use a hook with a stopper.
Forward pass too tight — the return pass becomes difficult.

name: Overlay Crochet Mandala
shortDescription: A detailed mandala using overlay crochet. Multiple layers of post stitches create a 3D effect.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses overlay crochet with post stitches, popcorn stitches, and multiple color layers.

yarn.notes: 6 colors of DK cotton, 25-35 yards each.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for a mandala.

instructions: **Rounds 1-5 (center, Color A):** Chain 8, join. 16 dc into ring. Work 4 rounds of increases.
**Rounds 6-10 (layer 1, Color B):** Work fpdc around posts from rounds 1-5 to create a raised petal layer on top of the center.
**Rounds 11-15 (layer 2, Color C):** Work another petal layer offset from layer 1. Add popcorn stitches at petal tips.
**Rounds 16-20 (background, Color D):** Work dc in the spaces between petals to fill the background.
**Rounds 21-25 (outer border, Colors E & F):** Alternate shell stitch and picot border.
**Finishing:** Block aggressively. Pin each petal flat while drying.
beginnerTips: Overlay crochet creates depth by layering stitches on top of previous rounds.
Post stitches grab the post of stitches several rounds below.
Each color layer is a separate round — never cut a color until all layers using it are complete.
commonMistakes: Fpdc worked too tightly — the petals will pull the fabric inward.
Forgetting to skip stitches behind the overlay — the base round needs to have extra stitches.

name: Amigurumi Turtle
shortDescription: A cute amigurumi turtle with a patterned shell. Quick and adorable.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses amigurumi techniques: magic ring, increases, decreases, and sewing.

yarn.notes: Green and brown DK yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical for toys.

instructions: **Body (brown):** Magic ring, 6 sc. Increase to 30 sts. Work even 8 rounds. Stuff. Decrease to close.
**Shell (green):** Magic ring, 6 sc. Increase to 36 sts over 6 rounds. Work even 6 rounds. Decrease slightly to fit over body.
**Legs (make 4, green):** Magic ring, 6 sc. Increase to 12 sts. Work even 4 rounds. Decrease to close.
**Head (green):** Magic ring, 6 sc. Increase to 18 sts. Work even 5 rounds. Insert safety eyes. Decrease to close.
**Tail (green):** Magic ring, 6 sc. Work even 3 rounds. Decrease to close.
**Assembly:** Sew head, legs, and tail to body. Sew shell on top of body, leaving a small opening. Add extra stuffing to shell if needed. Close shell opening.
**Finishing:** Weave in all ends.
beginnerTips: Use a stitch marker on every round for amigurumi.
Safety eyes should be secured before closing the head.
The shell should be slightly domed — overstuff it a bit.
commonMistakes: Legs placed asymmetrically — measure placement before sewing.
Eyes too close together — leave 4-5 stitches between them.

name: Amigurumi Star
shortDescription: A 5-pointed star toy or decoration. Soft and baby-safe without plastic parts.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses single crochet with shaping for 5 identical points.

yarn.notes: Yellow or gold yarn.

gauge.notes: Gauge is not critical.

instructions: **Center:** Magic ring, 6 sc. Increase to 30 sc over 5 rounds.
**Point 1:** Sc in next 6 stitches. Turn and work back, decreasing at each edge: sc in 6, turn; sc in next 4, turn; sc in next 2; fasten off.
**Points 2-5:** Skip 0 stitches after Point 1, join yarn in the next stitch. Repeat the point shaping. (5 points total, 6 stitches per point).
**Backing:** Make a second star but do NOT stuff. Place both stars together, wrong sides facing.
**Joining:** Sc through both layers around the entire star, stuffing lightly as you go.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends.
beginnerTips: Each point is 6 stitches wide at the base — mark them with stitch markers.
The second star is the backing — no need to shape as carefully.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to stuff before the closing round.
Points not evenly spaced — count 6 stitches per point.

name: Entrelac Crochet Scarf
shortDescription: A scarf made with the entrelac technique, creating a woven basketweave of interlocking diamonds.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses entrelac technique with diamonds worked in tiers; requires understanding of foundation rows and pick-up stitches.

yarn.notes: 2 contrasting colors, 175yds each.

gauge.notes: Gauge determines diamond size.

instructions: **Foundation tier (Color A):** Chain 30. *Sc in 2nd chain, hdc in next, dc in next 2, tr in next 4, dc in next 2, hdc in next, sc in next.* Repeat across. (3 diamonds in the tier).
**Tier 2 (Color B):** Pick up stitches along the top edge of Tier 1. Work diamonds in the opposite direction (pointing up). Each diamond is built by decreasing at each edge.
**Tiers 3-10:** Alternate colors each tier. The diamonds interlock to create a woven fabric.
**Finishing:** Weave in ends. Block to shape.
beginnerTips: Entrelac looks complex but is just repeating the same diamond shape.
Use stitch markers at the top of each diamond to track tiers.
The pick-up edge is the most important part — keep it even.
commonMistakes: Diamond edges uneven — each decrease must be consistent.
Losing count of stitches per diamond.

name: Lace Tablecloth Centerpiece
shortDescription: A round lace tablecloth centerpiece (30 inches). A true heirloom project with intricate stitchwork.

difficulty.reasoning: Uses chains, double crochet, treble crochet, picots, and complex increases over 45+ rounds.

yarn.notes: Mercerized cotton thread (size 10), white or ecru.

gauge.notes: Gauge is somewhat critical for final size.

instructions: **Center:** Chain 12, join. Work 24 dc into ring.
**Rounds 1-15:** Increase evenly by 12 stitches each round. The center grows flat.
**Rounds 16-30:** Begin the lace pattern: chain loops, picots, and treble clusters form a floral motif that repeats around the circle.
**Rounds 31-45:** The lace becomes more open with chain arches and scalloped edges.
**Border:** *7 tr in next chain space, skip 2, sl st in next.* Repeat around.
**Finishing:** Fasten off. Block aggressively — pin every scallop flat. Starch firmly. Allow to dry completely.
beginnerTips: This is a long-term project — work on it in sections.
Use a stitch marker at the start of each round; 45+ rounds is easy to lose track of.
Blocking is the most important step — an unblocked tablecloth looks like a crumpled mess.
Starching is essential for a tablecloth to lie flat.
commonMistakes: Not counting stitches between increases — the tablecloth won't lie flat.
Skipping the blocking step — don't skip it!
Tension changes over the 45 rounds causing uneven sections.
